purpose: Converts text to capital letters.

example.explain: Fixes a PAN typed in small letters.

tip: Paste back as values (⌘ + Control + V) to replace the original column.

name: VALUE
purpose: Converts text that looks like a number into a real number.

example.explain: Turns an amount stored as text into a number you can add up.

tip: A quicker fix for a whole column is to multiply by 1 or use the green error triangle's Convert to Number.

name: VALUETOTEXT
purpose: Converts any value into text.

args.name: format
args.desc: 0 concise (default), 1 strict with quotes around text

example.explain: Returns the number 2500 as the text "2500".

tip: Format 1 wraps text in quotes, useful when building formula strings.

name: VAR
purpose: Older function for the variance of a sample.

example.explain: Sample variance of branch sales, same as VAR.S.

tip: Use VAR.S in new workbooks.

name: VAR.P
purpose: Returns the variance when your data is the whole population.

example.explain: Population variance of sales across all five branches.

tip: Variance is in squared units; STDEV.P is usually easier to explain.

name: VAR.S
purpose: Returns the variance of a sample, the average squared distance from the mean.

example.explain: Sample variance of branch sales; its square root is STDEV.S.

tip: Use .S for a sample and .P when you have every value.

name: VARA
purpose: Returns the sample variance, counting text as 0 and TRUE as 1.

example.explain: Counts Absent as 0 when calculating the variance of scores.

name: VARP
purpose: Older function for the variance of a whole population.

example.explain: Population variance of branch sales, same as VAR.P.

tip: Use VAR.P in new workbooks.

name: VARPA
purpose: Returns the population variance, counting text as 0 and TRUE as 1.

example.explain: Population variance of the four scores with Absent counted as 0.

name: VDB
purpose: Returns declining-balance depreciation for any period, switching to straight line when that is larger.

args.name: salvage
args.desc: Value at the end of its life

args.name: start_period
args.desc: Start of the period to calculate

args.name: end_period
args.desc: End of the period to calculate

args.name: no_switch
args.desc: TRUE stops the switch to straight line

example.explain: First-year double declining depreciation on a ₹5,00,000 asset.

tip: Use fractional periods (0 to 0.5) for an asset bought mid-year.

name: VLOOKUP
purpose: Finds a value in the first column of a table and returns a value from a column to its right.

args.name: lookup_value
args.desc: The value to find, such as a product code

args.name: table_array
args.desc: The table, with the lookup column first

args.name: col_index_num
args.desc: Which column of the table to return, counting from 1

args.name: range_lookup
args.desc: FALSE for exact match; TRUE or blank for approximate (needs sorted data)

example.explain: Finds code P102 and returns its price from the third column.

tip: Always type FALSE for exact match; leaving it blank gives wrong answers on unsorted data.

name: VSTACK
purpose: Stacks ranges on top of each other into one list.

example.explain: Combines two branch lists into one column.

tip: Use it to combine the same table from monthly sheets: =VSTACK(Apr!A2:D50,May!A2:D50).

name: WEBSERVICE
purpose: Returns data from a web address (URL) on the internet.

args.name: url
args.desc: The web address to call, up to 2,048 characters

example.result: the raw text the service returns, for example 84.12
example.explain: Calls a web API and shows its reply; works only in Excel for Windows with internet, not on a Mac.

tip: On a Mac use Power Query (Data > Get Data > From Web) or the Stocks data type instead.

name: WEEKDAY
purpose: Returns the day of the week of a date as a number.

example.explain: With Monday as 1, Independence Day 2026 falls on a Saturday, day 6.

tip: Flag weekends with =WEEKDAY(A2,2)>5.

name: WEEKNUM
purpose: Returns the week number of the year for a date.

args.name: return_type
args.desc: 1 weeks start Sunday (default), 2 Monday, 21 ISO method

example.explain: 15 August 2026 falls in week 33 when weeks start on Sunday.

tip: Use return_type 21 or ISOWEEKNUM to match ISO week numbers used by many global teams.

name: WEIBULL
purpose: Older function for the Weibull distribution, used in reliability analysis.

args.name: cumulative
args.desc: TRUE for cumulative, FALSE for density

example.explain: Probability that a part fails within 105 hours.

tip: Use WEIBULL.DIST in new workbooks.

name: WEIBULL.DIST
purpose: Returns the Weibull distribution, often used to model time to failure.

args.name: cumulative
args.desc: TRUE for cumulative, FALSE for density

example.explain: Probability that a machine part fails within 105 hours.

name: WORKDAY
purpose: Returns the date a set number of working days away, skipping weekends and holidays.

args.name: days
args.desc: Working days to add (negative to go back)

args.name: holidays
args.desc: A range of holiday dates to skip

example.explain: Three working days after 30 Sep, skipping Gandhi Jayanti and the weekend, is 6 Oct.

tip: Keep a named range of company holidays and use it in every WORKDAY formula.

name: WORKDAY.INTL
purpose: Returns a date a set number of working days away, with weekends you choose.

args.name: weekend
args.desc: Weekend code, such as 11 for Sunday only, or a 7-character string like "0000001"

args.name: holidays
args.desc: A range of holiday dates to skip

example.explain: For a shop open six days a week, three working days after 30 Sep is 5 Oct.

tip: Code 11 (Sunday only) suits most Indian shops and factories with a six-day week.

name: WRAPCOLS
purpose: Wraps a single row or column of values into columns of a set height.

args.name: vector
args.desc: The single row or column to wrap

example.explain: Splits four names into columns of two, for example two teams.

tip: Use pad_with "" to avoid #N/A when the list does not divide evenly.

name: WRAPROWS
purpose: Wraps a single row or column of values into rows of a set width.

args.name: vector
args.desc: The single row or column to wrap

example.explain: Lays the names out two per row, like seating pairs.

tip: Handy for turning a long exported list of field and value pairs back into a table.

name: XIRR
purpose: Returns the annual return for cash flows on irregular dates, such as mutual fund SIPs and redemptions.

args.name: values
args.desc: Cash flows; investments negative, money received positive

args.name: dates
args.desc: The date of each cash flow

example.explain: Annual return on two investments of ₹1,00,000 and ₹50,000 that are worth ₹1,65,000 on 31 Mar 2026.

tip: Enter money you put in as negative and the current value as a positive final flow.

name: XLOOKUP
purpose: Finds a value in one range and returns the matching item from another, in any direction.

args.name: if_not_found
args.desc: What to show if there is no match

args.name: match_mode
args.desc: 0 exact (default), -1 exact or next smaller, 1 exact or next larger, 2 wildcard

args.name: search_mode
args.desc: 1 first to last (default), -1 last to first, 2 or -2 binary search

example.explain: Finds code P103 and returns the product name, or Not found if the code is missing.

tip: Return several columns at once by giving a wider return range, such as B2:C4.

name: XMATCH
purpose: Returns the position of an item in a list, with more match options than MATCH.

args.name: match_mode
args.desc: 0 exact (default), -1 next smaller, 1 next larger, 2 wildcard

args.name: search_mode
args.desc: 1 first to last (default), -1 last to first, 2 or -2 binary

example.explain: Notebook is the second item in the product list.

tip: Exact match is the default, unlike MATCH which defaults to approximate.

name: XNPV
purpose: Returns the net present value of cash flows on irregular dates.

args.name: values
args.desc: Cash flows, the first usually an outflow

args.name: dates
args.desc: The date of each cash flow

example.explain: At a 10% discount rate the investment is worth about ₹2,372 more than it cost, in today's money.

tip: Unlike NPV, the first cash flow is not discounted, because it happens on the start date.

name: XOR
purpose: Returns TRUE when an odd number of conditions are TRUE, such as exactly one of two.

example.explain: TRUE because exactly one of the two answers is Yes, which is the valid case.

tip: With more than two conditions XOR means an odd number are TRUE, not exactly one.

name: YEAR
purpose: Returns the year from a date.

example.explain: Pulls the joining year out of a date.

tip: For the Indian financial year use =YEAR(A2)+(MONTH(A2)>=4)-1 to get the starting year.

name: YEARFRAC
purpose: Returns the fraction of a year between two dates.

example.explain: The first half of FY 2026-27 is just under half a year on an actual day count.

tip: Use basis 1 for exact tenure or interest; the default 30/360 can differ slightly.

name: YIELD
purpose: Returns the yield of a bond that pays periodic interest.
syntax: YIELD(settlement, maturity, rate, pr, redemption, frequency, [basis])

example.explain: Yield on a 7.1% government bond bought at ₹98.50 with five years left.

name: YIELDDISC
purpose: Returns the annual yield of a discounted security, such as commercial paper.

example.explain: Yield on six-month commercial paper bought at ₹97.

name: YIELDMAT
purpose: Returns the annual yield of a security that pays interest at maturity.

example.explain: Yield on a 7% instrument that pays all interest at maturity, bought at ₹99.

name: Z.TEST
purpose: Returns the one-tailed p-value of a z-test against a hypothesised average.

args.name: sigma
args.desc: Known population standard deviation; sample value used if left out

example.explain: Small p-value: the average customer rating is very likely above 4.

tip: For a two-tailed p-value use =2*MIN(Z.TEST(A2:A6,4),1-Z.TEST(A2:A6,4)).

name: ZTEST
purpose: Older function for the one-tailed p-value of a z-test.

example.explain: Same result as Z.TEST for the customer ratings.

tip: Use Z.TEST in new workbooks.
